pageReviews.summary: The page has 5 actionable findings. The main risk is that R6 ballot4 currently gives conflicting GET-invocation criteria and did not fully apply the `FHIR-41220` cleanup, leaving implementers without a single clear rule for URL/query parameters.

narrative.analysis:
H-001: GET invocation criteria conflict across the page

Evidence: `fhir-spec-search/trees/source/hl7.fhir.core/6.0.0-ballot4-5d67a34a13a5/source/operations.html:63-64`, `:98-102`, `:238-241`; `FHIR-51046`; `FHIR-56194`; commit `d542f8a98ce80fed9a951b76190bb8379ebc09f5`; Zulip `#implementers > Understanding GET invoked extended operations`.

Problem: one section says GET applies when parameters are primitive datatypes with no extensions, another says GET applies to parameters whose data type has a corresponding search type, and the Operation Request section still says all operation parameters must be primitive types.

Why it matters: Identifier and Reference are explicitly permitted by the newer `FHIR-51046` rule, but readers can still conclude they are prohibited by the primitive-only paragraphs.

Recommended next step: align all GET-invocation paragraphs to one rule and add/point to a clear table or definition for "has a corresponding search type"; triage against `FHIR-56194`.

Intent-vs-implementation context: `H-001` and `H-002` are the material mismatches: `FHIR-51046`/`FHIR-56194` point to a search-type criterion that was not propagated to all GET text, and `FHIR-41220` explicitly requested removal/replacement of `simple parameters` but the current source still contains it.
narrative.whyItMatters: Identifier and Reference are explicitly permitted by the newer `FHIR-51046` rule, but readers can still conclude they are prohibited by the primitive-only paragraphs.
narrative.recommendedNextStep: align all GET-invocation paragraphs to one rule and add/point to a clear table or definition for "has a corresponding search type"; triage against `FHIR-56194`.

findings.title: no-output operation responses need the later clarification

narrative.problem: R6 ballot4 says the body can be omitted when there are zero output parameters, but `FHIR-56007` later resolved that successful operations with no out parameters may return either an empty body or an empty Parameters resource and should update both sections.
narrative.analysis:
H-003: no-output operation responses need the later clarification

Evidence: `fhir-spec-search/trees/source/hl7.fhir.core/6.0.0-ballot4-5d67a34a13a5/source/operations.html:85-91` and `:270-292`; `FHIR-24869`; later `FHIR-56007`.

Problem: R6 ballot4 says the body can be omitted when there are zero output parameters, but `FHIR-56007` later resolved that successful operations with no out parameters may return either an empty body or an empty Parameters resource and should update both sections.

Why it matters: clients and servers can interpret zero-output success responses differently.

Recommended next step: apply the `FHIR-56007` clarification to both the execution and response sections.

Overlooked/newly noticed context: `H-003`, `E-001`, and `E-002` are current-page problems visible after reading the full R6 ballot4 source. `E-001` did not show a matching Jira hit for `For eample`; `E-002` is already tracked by `FHIR-45277`.
narrative.whyItMatters: clients and servers can interpret zero-output success responses differently.
narrative.recommendedNextStep: apply the `FHIR-56007` clarification to both the execution and response sections.
